condition: Testicular torsion presenting as groin pain
summary: 14-year-old boy with 3 hours of sudden severe right groin and scrotal pain and vomiting, high-riding tender testis, absent cremasteric reflex. Torsion until proven otherwise: emergency scrotal exploration; ultrasound must not delay theatre.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden pain in the right groin and testicle
inputs.hpi: Woke 3 hours ago with sudden severe pain in the right groin going down into the right testicle. Vomited twice. No trauma. No urinary symptoms. Mother thought it was a hernia.

exam.msk: Genitalia: right testis high-riding with horizontal lie, exquisitely tender, mildly swollen scrotum; absent right cremasteric reflex. Left testis normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right testicular torsion (clinical diagnosis)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right testicular torsion until proven otherwise — 3 h, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex. Emergency scrotal exploration and bilateral fixation; do not delay for ultrasound.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = inguinal hernia, appendicitis, epididymo-orchitis: testicular_torsion (prior 0.01) is outranked although testicular_pain/scrotal_swelling are applied; vomiting and "sudden" onset are not mapped to features. The safety prompt and the ICD plan (N44.00 → testicular_torsion) are correct.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Model P(feature | not disease) or use a low default sensitivity (e.g. <=0.05) for features outside a disease's system; restrict the candidate set by the presenting system (breast / neck / groin).

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: As above: torsion not in the PANE top 3; epididymo-orchitis ranks above it.

mustExclude.note: The mother's label ("hernia") and the groin template must not produce a hernia plan.

guideline.name: EAU/ESPU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology — acute scrotum
guideline.section: Testicular torsion: clinical diagnosis, Doppler ultrasound must not delay surgery, urgent scrotal exploration
guideline.citation: Radmayr C, Bogaert G, Burgu B, et al. EAU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology. EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition. Section: Acute scrotum in children.

rationale: Groin mimic with a 6-hour salvage window. The presenting words are "groin" and the only groin CC template is the hernia one; the scrotal findings are recorded where the web prompt engine reads them (extremities exam) and as chips.
